svg.aria-label: Classification of non-coding RNA and two misconceptions: the definition as RNA not used as a protein template, why that must be distinguished from having no function, the classes arranged by size and function, and the division between the basic machinery group and the expression-regulating group.
svg.text: Definition: RNA that is NOT used as a template to make protein. That is the whole definition — not a class by function, size or mechanism.
Two misconceptions, in opposite directions
1 "non-coding" is not "non-functional"
rRNA and tRNA are non-coding, and without them there is
no translation at all. Not being translated means the work
is done without going through a protein: the RNA is the product.
2 being transcribed is not having a function
Much of the genome is transcribed to some degree. Some of
that is a by-product of transcription itself. Function has
to be shown separately — see section 10.
The classes
Part of the basic machinery (structural)
rRNA 1.5 to 5 kb ribosome structure and catalysis
tRNA 76 to 90 nt amino acid delivery, codon reading
snRNA 100 to 300 nt spliceosome components (U1, U2, U4-6)
snoRNA 60 to 300 nt guides rRNA modification
rRNA alone is about 80 percent of cellular RNA.
Regulators of expression — this lesson
miRNA about 22 nt represses translation, promotes decay
siRNA 21 to 23 nt cleaves a fully complementary mRNA
piRNA 24 to 31 nt silences transposons, germ cells
lncRNA over 200 nt very diverse
lncRNA is defined by SIZE: a leftover category, not a function.
